subject: Cloud Computing
title: Message Queues and Decoupling
description: A fast breakdown of Message Queues and Decoupling for builders.

hook.text: A user uploads a video. Processing takes 10 minutes. Do they wait? No — a message queue handles it in the background.

buildup.text: Message queues let services communicate asynchronously. The sender drops a message; the receiver picks it up later.

discovery.text: AWS SQS, RabbitMQ, and Apache Kafka are popular choices. Each handles different scales and patterns.

twist.text: Queues add latency by design. Data isn't processed instantly — it waits in line. That delay must be acceptable.

climax.text: Queues absorb traffic spikes like a buffer. Producers can burst while consumers process at their own pace.

punchline.text: Queues absorb the burst. Consumers work at their own speed.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of using message queues?
options: Services communicate asynchronously, absorbing traffic spikes
Messages are processed instantly with zero latency
Queues eliminate the need for databases entirely

details.summary: Message queues let services communicate asynchronously by placing messages in a buffer that consumers process at their own pace. This decouples producers from consumers, absorbs traffic spikes, and ensures messages are not lost if a consumer is temporarily down.
details.whyItMatters: Synchronous calls between services create tight coupling and cascading failures. Queues buffer demand, smooth traffic spikes, and make systems more resilient to partial outages.
takeaways: Producers and consumers operate independently via a queue
Queues absorb traffic spikes and smooth processing load

faq.question: What is the difference between a queue and a topic?
faq.answer: A queue delivers each message to exactly one consumer, useful for work distribution. A topic delivers each message to all subscribers, useful for fan-out notifications. Some systems like Kafka combine both models through consumer groups.

faq.question: How do you handle poison messages?
faq.answer: A poison message repeatedly fails processing and blocks the queue. Dead letter queues capture messages that exceed a retry limit so they can be inspected without blocking other messages. Alerting on dead letter queue depth catches problems early.
